A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KARE and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably across appendix and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original mortality and readmission experiments on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, component ablations, training-loss analyses, and prediction case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds fine-tuned RAG results, expert evaluations of generated reasoning, and model resource comparisons.

M1.justification: The three-source KG construction, semantic clustering, hierarchical community indexing, DGRA retrieval, rationale generation, and multitask fine-tuning remain unchanged. New construction examples document the existing procedure; the suggested reasoning-consistency verification is future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV for next-visit mortality and 15-day readmission prediction, and retain the synthetic MIMIC-III case study. Expert ratings assess existing test-set outputs without introducing a new patient population, prediction task, or input scenario.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds fine-tuned Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 Backbone and Classic RAG comparators across both datasets and tasks. Backbone results already appeared in v1's Table 3, but its participation in the main comparison is new. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: Appendix H introduces a distinct expert-evaluation protocol: one MD and three MD students assess 100 test-set reasoning chains on five 1–5 scales, with 35 correct and 15 incorrect predictions per task. Appendix I adds resource comparisons measuring time to optimal validation performance. Existing dataset splits, preprocessing, and training configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis through expert assessment of reasoning quality and failure cases in Appendix H, performance-versus-resource analyses in Appendix I, and concrete KG-extraction examples in Appendix B.4. Existing component, retrieval, knowledge-source, and multitask ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains averaging over 30 ML, 10 LM+ML, and 3 LLM runs; Table 3 retains three seeded runs. The new expert ratings and resource plots introduce no confidence intervals, significance tests, inter-rater agreement estimates, or other uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are retained. Newly reported fine-tuned Classic RAG Macro-F1 scores are 51.4/59.9 for MIMIC-III mortality/readmission and 83.8/52.1 for MIMIC-IV. Backbone scores repeat v1's ablation results. Figure 18 adds expert ratings and lower scores for incorrect predictions, while Figures 19–20 add resource measurements, substantially broadening reported outcomes.

T1.justification: Existing KG definitions, retrieval equations, and algorithms are unchanged. However, new Appendix E, Equation 8 explicitly defines Macro-F1 using positive-class precision and recall without class averaging, introducing a substantive mathematical definition error. This does not establish that the metric actually computed in the experiments changed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, headline improvement percentages, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims and scope. The conclusion adds a pointer to human evaluation without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix H adds interpretations concerning missing demographics, reasoning–prediction contradictions, and possible consistency verification. It also asserts superiority to clinicians without reporting a clinician prediction comparison. Appendix E adds reasons for excluding AUROC/AUPRC. The main results discussion and Appendix A limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix I adds per-model parameter counts and training-duration information beyond v1's broad training-time estimate. Hardware, fine-tuning hyperparameters, software, prompts, code-access statement, and promised processed-data release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds MedRetriever, EHR-KnowGen, ClinicalBench, and broader rationale-distillation citations. Section 3.1.3 removes the explicit contrast with GraphRAG. These are localized extensions and positioning refinements; the overall research framing remains.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, expands related-work and metric explanations, adds acknowledgements, and updates the publication header. New appendix sections cause renumbering of retained case studies, prompts, and notation material; the main narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds KG-construction example Figures 7–9, the four-panel expert-rating Figure 18, and resource-comparison Figures 19–20. Table 2 gains a fine-tuned-model group. These materially expand the visual evidence, while existing case-study and prompt figures are retained under new numbers.

improvement.justification: The fine-tuned RAG comparison, expert reasoning assessment, and resource plots provide a modest net improvement in evidential support and transparency. The expert study also exposes reasoning–prediction inconsistencies previously unexamined. Benefits are limited by absent baseline reasoning ratings and inter-rater reliability reporting, the new Macro-F1 definition error, and the unsupported assertion of superiority to clinicians.
